newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, widen on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, widen on Tuesday.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities widened to Treasuries for the first time in several days on Tuesday, but fixed-income analysts said the market still looks attractive compared to Treasuries.
Pass-throughs rose 1/32 to 4/32 overall in the morning and held near those levels most of the afternoon, with discount coupons performing best. The 10-year Treasury note was up 6/32 late in the day.
Treasuries rose on retail, hedge fund and central bank activity, bond market analysts said.
Traders and analysts said some fund managers have underweighted government securities and overweighted mortgage-backeds in the past week, possibly explaining the past week's narrowing trend.

For example, 69 percent of respondents to the MCM MoneyWatch Inc weekly asset allocation survey reported overweighting mortgage-backeds in the week ended August 24, according to an MCM report. The survey polls 38 money managers who control assets of about $90 billion.
The Conference Board's Tuesday morning report on consumer confidence knocked both markets off their early highs.
Confidence rose to 109.4 in August from a revised 107.0 in July. Wall Street economists had expected confidence to decline.
Late on Tuesday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were up 3/32 at 100-21/32, yielding 119 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were up 2/32 at 100-17/32, and FHLMCs were up 1/32 at 100-19/32.
